clinical_knowledge.topic: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes confirming the diabetes type before starting metformin, dietary changes, and regular HbA1c monitoring, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue

Key HPI features: A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic with increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Type 1 diabetes without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: young age of onset with significant weight loss or ketosis, signs of diabetic ketoacidosis (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, kussmaul breathing, fruity breath), or very high presenting glucose with dehydration or altered mental status.
management_principles: Confirm diabetes with plasma glucose and/or HbA1c, assess for ketosis and acute illness, and distinguish type 1 diabetes or other diabetes types before selecting treatment
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue. HPI: insulin resistance, obesity.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
reference_soap.assessment: Symptomatic hyperglycemia is suspected; diabetes type and acute metabolic complications require assessment before labeling this as type 2 diabetes.
reference_soap.plan: Confirm diabetes with plasma glucose and HbA1c, obtain electrolytes/renal function, and assess blood or urine ketones and acid-base status when clinically indicated. Distinguish type 1 diabetes or other diabetes types before selecting treatment. Start lifestyle and pharmacologic therapy according to the confirmed diabetes type, glycemic severity, renal function, and pregnancy status; arrange prompt follow-up.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
Implement evidence-based management plan: Metformin, dietary changes, regular HbA1c checks

teaching.one_liner: Insulin resistance, often related to obesity, causing increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue.
red_flags: Young age of onset with significant weight loss or ketosis — raises concern for type 1 diabetes or LADA rather than type 2
Signs of diabetic ketoacidosis (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath) — a medical emergency
Very high presenting glucose with dehydration or altered mental status — raises concern for hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state
